A study by Kessler et al. (2012) compared a dose-titration strategy to a fixed dose of trospium chloride in patients with NDO.
The study was a 12-week, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial.
Patients were randomly assigned to receive either a fixed dose of 20 mg three times daily or a dose-titration strategy.
The primary outcome was the change from baseline in the number of incontinence episodes per 24 hours.
The dose-titration strategy resulted in a significantly greater reduction in the number of incontinence episodes compared to the fixed dose (p<0.001).
